items.e: Low-velocity gunshot fractures with small wounds can be managed with local wound care, a short antibiotic course and fracture treatment as for a closed injury; high-velocity or contaminated wounds need formal debridement.

items.q: Which surgical approach for acetabular fractures carries the highest risk of heterotopic ossification?
items.e: Extensive stripping of the outer iliac muscles in the extended iliofemoral approach (and to a lesser extent Kocher-Langenbeck) gives the highest rate of heterotopic ossification; the anterior intrapelvic approaches have the lowest.

items.q: According to the fracture-related infection (FRI) consensus definition, which finding is a confirmatory criterion?
o: A fistula or sinus tract communicating with the bone or implant
A raised CRP at 2 weeks after surgery
items.e: Confirmatory FRI criteria are a fistula, sinus or wound breakdown communicating with bone or implant, purulent drainage or pus, phenotypically identical organisms in two or more deep samples, and specific histology; raised inflammatory markers and fever are only suggestive.

items.q: During insertion of supra-acetabular (AIIS) pins for an anterior pelvic external fixator, which nerve is most at risk?
items.e: The lateral femoral cutaneous nerve passes close to the anterior superior and anterior inferior iliac spines and is at risk from pins and incisions in this area; blunt dissection down to bone reduces the risk.

items.q: On the true lateral sacral view during iliosacral screw insertion, the guidewire must stay inferior and posterior to the iliac cortical density (alar slope) mainly to avoid injury to the:
o: S1 nerve root in its foramen
L5 nerve root on the sacral ala
items.e: The L5 root crosses the anterior sacral ala, whose slope is marked by the iliac cortical density; a screw passing anterior or superior to it can exit the ala and injure L5.

items.q: Which feature distinguishes a cervical flexion teardrop fracture from an extension teardrop avulsion?
o: It is a stable avulsion of the anteroinferior corner of C2
It typically occurs in the elderly after a minor fall
It never involves the posterior ligaments
It is a highly unstable injury often causing anterior cord syndrome
items.e: Flexion teardrop fractures (usually C4-C6) combine an anteroinferior body fragment with retrolisthesis of the posterior body and posterior ligament disruption, making them unstable and frequently associated with anterior cord syndrome.

items.q: A labourer feels a sudden pop between the shoulder blades while shovelling; radiographs show an isolated avulsion of the C7 spinous process. Management is:
o: Symptomatic treatment, as this is a stable injury
items.e: A clay-shoveller's fracture is an avulsion of the C7 or T1 spinous process by trapezius and rhomboids; it is stable and treated symptomatically.

items.q: In Dickman's classification of transverse atlantal ligament injuries, a type I (midsubstance ligament) disruption is best managed by:
o: Halo vest, which heals most cases
items.e: Type I (ligamentous) TAL injuries do not heal with external immobilisation and need C1-C2 fusion, whereas type II (bony avulsion of the TAL insertion) injuries heal with a collar or halo in about three-quarters of cases.

items.q: Ossification of the posterior longitudinal ligament has its highest prevalence in which population?
items.e: Cervical OPLL is found in about 2-4% of Japanese adults and is common across East Asia, compared with under 1% in white populations.

items.q: According to Resnick's criteria, diffuse idiopathic skeletal hyperostosis (DISH) requires:
o: Flowing ossification along the anterolateral aspect of at least four contiguous vertebral bodies, with preserved disc height and no sacroiliac ankylosis
Marginal syndesmophytes with squaring of vertebrae
Disc space narrowing with vacuum phenomenon at three levels
items.e: DISH is defined by flowing anterolateral ossification over at least four contiguous vertebrae, relative preservation of disc height and absence of facet or sacroiliac ankylosis, distinguishing it from ankylosing spondylitis and spondylosis.

items.q: A 50-year-old has thoracic myelopathy from a calcified central T8-T9 disc herniation. Which approach should be avoided?
items.e: Laminectomy for a central thoracic disc requires cord retraction in the narrow thoracic canal and had high rates of neurological deterioration; anterior, lateral or posterolateral approaches are used instead.

items.q: According to Hilibrand's long-term follow-up after anterior cervical arthrodesis, symptomatic adjacent segment disease develops at a rate of about:
items.e: Hilibrand reported symptomatic adjacent segment disease at about 2.9% per year, with a predicted prevalence of about 26% at 10 years after anterior cervical fusion.

items.q: Compared with fresh-frozen allograft, freeze-dried (lyophilised) allograft bone is:
o: Weaker in compression and torsion, but least immunogenic
items.e: Freeze-drying removes water, lowering immunogenicity and allowing room-temperature storage, but it reduces mechanical strength; fresh grafts are the most immunogenic.

items.q: In the BESTT trial, adding rhBMP-2 on an absorbable collagen sponge to intramedullary nailing of open tibial fractures resulted in:
o: Fewer secondary interventions, faster healing and fewer infections
items.e: BESTT (2002) showed that 1.5 mg/mL rhBMP-2 reduced secondary interventions for delayed union, accelerated healing and lowered infection rates in open tibial fractures, leading to its approval for this use.

items.q: A trial reports a relative risk of revision of 0.80 with a 95% confidence interval of 0.55 to 1.15. How should this be interpreted?
o: The result is not statistically significant at the 5% level because the interval includes 1
The study must have been underpowered by definition
items.e: A 95% confidence interval for a ratio that includes 1 (no effect) means the difference is not statistically significant at p < 0.05; it cannot by itself prove the study was underpowered.

items.q: After a complete nerve transection, fibrillation potentials on EMG of the denervated muscle first appear at about:
items.e: Fibrillations and positive sharp waves appear 2-3 weeks after denervation once Wallerian degeneration is complete, so EMG is most informative at 3-4 weeks after injury.

items.q: A 30-year-old has an axonotmetic radial nerve injury about 20 cm proximal to the motor point of the first muscle expected to recover. Assuming regeneration of about 1 mm a day, reinnervation is expected after roughly:
items.e: Axons regenerate at roughly 1 mm a day (about 1 inch a month), so 200 mm needs around 200 days, about 6-7 months, before the first muscle shows recovery.

items.q: Delayed-onset muscle soreness peaking 24-72 hours after unaccustomed exercise is most associated with which type of contraction?
items.e: Eccentric contractions (muscle lengthening under load, e.g., downhill running) generate the highest forces per fibre and cause microtrauma that produces delayed-onset soreness peaking at 24-72 hours.

items.q: On CT, which tissue has an attenuation of about -100 Hounsfield units?
items.e: By definition water is 0 HU and air -1000 HU; fat is about -50 to -100 HU and cortical bone around +1000 HU or more.

items.q: In the HORIZON Recurrent Fracture Trial, annual zoledronic acid started within 90 days after hip fracture repair resulted in:
o: Fewer new clinical fractures and lower all-cause mortality
More atypical femoral fractures than placebo in the first year
items.e: HORIZON-RFT (2007) found zoledronic acid after hip fracture reduced new clinical fractures by about 35% and all-cause mortality by about 28%, without impairing fracture healing.

items.q: An intramedullary nail's diameter is increased from 10 mm to 12 mm with the same solid cross-sectional design. Its bending rigidity increases by approximately:
items.e: Bending rigidity depends on the area moment of inertia, which for a solid cylinder is proportional to the fourth power of the radius: (12/10)^4 ≈ 2.07.

items.q: Before a thigh tourniquet is inflated, the limb occlusion pressure (LOP) is measured at 150 mmHg. Using LOP-based recommendations, the appropriate cuff pressure is about:
items.e: LOP-based cuff pressure adds a safety margin of 40 mmHg for LOP up to 130, 60 mmHg for 131–190 and 80 mmHg above 190 mmHg, so 150 + 60 = 210 mmHg.

items.q: A glass laceration has visibly divided the median nerve at the wrist. Nerve conduction studies on day 3, stimulating the nerve distal to the laceration, show a normal thenar CMAP. The best explanation is:
o: The injury is a neurapraxia despite the visible division
Collateral sprouting has already reinnervated abductor pollicis brevis
Distal axons remain excitable until Wallerian degeneration is established (about 7–10 days), so studies should be repeated after 10–14 days
Volume conduction from ulnar-innervated muscles fully explains any normal CMAP
items.e: After transection the distal segment continues to conduct for roughly a week until Wallerian degeneration progresses, so early NCS cannot distinguish neurotmesis from milder injury.

items.q: Ten days after a 'Saturday night' radial nerve palsy, nerve conduction shows a normal CMAP when the radial nerve is stimulated distal to the spiral groove but a conduction block across the groove. This pattern indicates:
items.e: By day 10 axonal loss would reduce the distal CMAP; a preserved distal response with focal block across the lesion indicates demyelinating neurapraxia with a good prognosis.

items.q: During a gradually increasing voluntary contraction, motor units are recruited in order of size, smallest first (Henneman's size principle). The units recruited first are composed mainly of:
items.e: Small motor neurones with low thresholds innervate fatigue-resistant type I fibres, which are recruited first; large type II units are added as force demands rise.

items.q: When choosing a donor muscle for tendon transfer, the potential excursion (amplitude) of the muscle is proportional to its:
items.e: Excursion is proportional to fibre length, whereas force (strength) is proportional to physiological cross-sectional area.

items.q: A new MRI sign is positive in 45 of 50 knees with an arthroscopically confirmed meniscal tear and in 10 of 50 knees without a tear. Its specificity is:
items.e: Specificity = true negatives/(true negatives + false positives) = 40/50 = 80%; 90% is sensitivity, 82% the PPV (45/55) and 89% the NPV (40/45).

items.q: A clinical test for a scapholunate ligament tear has a sensitivity of 90% and a specificity of 80%. Its positive likelihood ratio is:
items.e: LR+ = sensitivity/(1 − specificity) = 0.9/0.2 = 4.5; 0.125 is the negative likelihood ratio (0.1/0.8).

items.q: In planning an RCT comparing two knee implants, the minimal clinically important difference used in the power calculation is halved while the standard deviation, alpha and power are unchanged. The required sample size will:
items.e: Sample size is inversely proportional to the square of the difference to be detected, so halving the difference quadruples the number of patients needed.

items.q: Two hip stem designs are compared using Kaplan–Meier survivorship curves with revision as the endpoint and patients censored at death or loss to follow-up. The appropriate test to compare the two curves is:
items.e: The log-rank test compares entire survival curves while accounting for censored data; multivariable adjustment uses Cox proportional hazards regression.

items.q: Pain scores (ordinal, non-normally distributed) are recorded in the same 40 patients before and six weeks after a nerve block. The appropriate test for the change is:
items.e: Paired, non-parametric data are analysed with the Wilcoxon signed-rank test; Mann–Whitney is for two independent groups and Kruskal–Wallis for three or more independent groups.

items.q: A study compares femoral anteversion measured by EOS 3D reconstruction with CT in the same patients to see whether the two methods can be used interchangeably. Agreement is best assessed with:
items.e: Correlation measures association, not agreement; Bland–Altman plots the differences against the means and gives limits of agreement for two methods measuring the same continuous quantity.

items.q: For serial standing whole-spine alignment imaging in an adolescent with scoliosis, the technique that gives the lowest radiation dose is:
o: Low-dose CT of the whole spine
items.e: EOS uses a slot-scanning detector that reduces dose several-fold compared with conventional radiography while giving simultaneous weight-bearing AP and lateral images.

items.q: A soft-tissue mass in the thigh is hyperintense on T1-weighted MRI and stays hyperintense on the fat-suppressed T1 sequence. The most likely content is:
items.e: Fat loses signal on fat suppression; T1 brightness persisting after fat suppression suggests methaemoglobin, proteinaceous fluid, melanin or gadolinium.

items.q: The most characteristic MRI feature of diffuse tenosynovial giant cell tumour (PVNS) of the knee is:
o: Frond-like synovial proliferation with fat signal on all sequences
Multiple uniform intra-articular bodies with ring-and-arc calcification
Synovial masses of low signal on T1 and T2 with blooming on gradient-echo images
A rim-enhancing collection with central diffusion restriction
items.e: Haemosiderin deposition causes low signal on all sequences and susceptibility blooming on gradient-echo; frond-like fat signal is lipoma arborescens.

items.q: To look for a deep hip joint effusion by ultrasound in an obese adult, the most appropriate transducer is:
o: Any probe, since frequency does not affect penetration
items.e: Lower frequencies penetrate deeper at the cost of resolution; high-frequency linear probes give fine detail only for superficial structures.

items.q: For surgical antibiotic prophylaxis before hip arthroplasty in a 130 kg adult, the recommended cefazolin dose is:
items.e: Guidelines (ASHP/IDSA/SIS) recommend cefazolin 2 g for adults and 3 g for those weighing 120 kg or more, given within 60 minutes before incision.

items.q: A patient develops ventricular arrhythmia after a bupivacaine fascia iliaca block. After starting CPR and airway management, the initial bolus of 20% lipid emulsion is:
items.e: ASRA guidance for local anaesthetic systemic toxicity is a 1.5 mL/kg bolus of 20% lipid emulsion (about 100 mL if over 70 kg), followed by an infusion.

items.q: In an RCT of clean-contaminated surgery (Darouiche, NEJM 2010), skin preparation with chlorhexidine–alcohol compared with povidone–iodine:
o: Had no effect on surgical site infection
Increased superficial infection due to skin reactions
items.e: Chlorhexidine–alcohol reduced overall surgical site infection (about 9.5% vs 16.1%), including superficial and deep incisional infections.

items.q: The master transcription factor required for osteoclast differentiation downstream of RANK signalling is:
items.e: RANKL–RANK signalling induces NFATc1, which drives osteoclast-specific genes such as TRAP and cathepsin K; RUNX2 and Osterix drive osteoblasts and SOX9 chondrocytes.

items.q: Differentiation of mesenchymal progenitors into chondrocytes is driven chiefly by which transcription factor?
items.e: SOX9 (with SOX5 and SOX6) directs chondrogenesis and type II collagen expression; RUNX2 is osteoblastic, PPAR-γ adipocytic and MyoD myogenic.

items.q: In adult articular cartilage, type X collagen is found mainly in the:
o: Calcified cartilage zone around hypertrophic chondrocytes
items.e: Type X collagen is a marker of chondrocyte hypertrophy, present in the calcified zone (and physeal hypertrophic zone); the pericellular matrix is rich in type VI.

items.q: The pericellular matrix of the chondron, which links chondrocytes to the surrounding matrix, is characteristically rich in which collagen?
items.e: Type VI collagen is concentrated around chondrocytes; type IX links type II fibrils, type XI regulates fibril diameter and type X marks hypertrophy.

items.q: Which feature distinguishes the synovial lining from a true epithelium?
o: The lining is always many cell layers thick
The lining cells are joined by tight junctions
It is avascular and nourished by diffusion
There is no basement membrane between the lining cells and the subintima
items.e: Synovial intima is one to three cell layers of type A and B synoviocytes without a basement membrane or tight junctions, over a vascular subintima.

items.q: A patient with right hip osteoarthritis must carry a heavy suitcase. To minimise the right hip joint reaction force it should be carried in the:
o: Either hand; side makes no difference
Left hand with a trunk lean to the left
items.e: A load in the ipsilateral hand creates a moment that assists the abductors, reducing abductor force and joint reaction force; a contralateral load increases it, unlike a cane, which is used contralaterally.

items.q: To use a 3.5 mm cortical screw as a lag screw by technique, the drill holes should be:
o: 3.5 mm gliding hole in the near cortex and 2.5 mm pilot hole in the far cortex
2.5 mm in the near cortex and 3.5 mm in the far cortex
items.e: Over-drilling the near cortex to the thread diameter lets the screw glide so that only the far cortex threads engage, producing interfragmentary compression.

items.q: Titanium alloy (Ti-6Al-4V) is not used for the femoral head bearing surface in hip arthroplasty mainly because of its:
o: Poor wear resistance and notch sensitivity
Susceptibility to galvanic corrosion with polyethylene
items.e: Titanium is biocompatible and has a low modulus, but its soft, notch-sensitive surface produces high wear debris against polyethylene.

items.q: During two-incision fasciotomy of the leg, the lateral incision is placed about 2 cm anterior to the fibula. The structure at particular risk in the distal part of this incision is the:
items.e: The superficial peroneal nerve pierces the crural fascia about 10–12 cm above the lateral malleolus and is at risk when the lateral and anterior compartments are released.

items.q: After two-incision fasciotomy for acute compartment syndrome of the leg, the compartment most often inadequately released is the:
items.e: The deep posterior compartment lies beneath soleus through the medial incision and requires detaching soleus from the tibia; it is the commonly missed compartment.

items.q: In an APC-II (Young–Burgess) pelvic ring injury, which ligaments remain intact?
items.e: APC-II disrupts the symphysis, anterior SI, sacrospinous and sacrotuberous ligaments, but the posterior SI ligaments remain intact, giving an 'open book' that is vertically stable.

items.q: The WHiTE 5 trial (NEJM 2022) compared cemented with modern uncemented hemiarthroplasty for displaced intracapsular hip fractures in older adults. Cemented hemiarthroplasty resulted in:
o: Worse quality of life with no difference in fractures
Slightly better quality of life and fewer periprosthetic fractures
More periprosthetic fractures but shorter operating time
items.e: Cemented stems gave a small improvement in EQ-5D at 4 months and fewer intraoperative/periprosthetic fractures, without increased mortality.

items.q: When nailing a proximal-third tibial shaft fracture, a blocking (Poller) screw to prevent valgus malalignment is placed in the proximal fragment:
o: Medial to the intended nail path
Anterior to the intended nail path
Medial to the nail in the distal fragment
Lateral to the intended nail path
items.e: Valgus occurs when the nail drifts laterally into the wide metaphysis; a lateral blocking screw narrows the canal and directs the nail medially. A posterior blocking screw prevents procurvatum.

items.q: A closed degloving (Morel-Lavallée) lesion overlies the planned Kocher-Langenbeck incision for an acetabular fracture. The recommended management is:
o: Debride and drain the lesion before or at definitive fixation because of high bacterial colonisation
Incise through it and proceed, as it does not affect infection risk
Single needle aspiration and immediate fixation
Delay fixation for 6 weeks until the lesion resolves
items.e: Fluid from these lesions is frequently culture-positive, so they are debrided and drained (open or percutaneously) to reduce deep infection after acetabular fixation.

items.q: In randomised trials of acute syndesmotic injury, dynamic suture-button fixation compared with a syndesmotic screw has shown:
o: Lower rates of malreduction and fewer implant removals
Higher rates of loss of reduction requiring revision
No difference in malreduction but more infections
items.e: The suture button permits physiological micromotion and tends to self-reduce, with less malreduction on CT and fewer routine removals than screw fixation.

items.q: A 40-year-old has an isolated Weber B fibular fracture; the medial clear space is normal on a weight-bearing radiograph. The appropriate treatment is:
o: ORIF of the fibula with a lag screw and neutralisation plate
Non-operative treatment with early weight-bearing in a boot or cast
items.e: A normal medial clear space on weight-bearing (or gravity stress) views indicates a stable injury that does well with functional non-operative treatment.

items.q: For displaced intra-articular calcaneal fractures, the sinus tarsi approach compared with the extensile lateral approach mainly offers:
o: Better direct visualisation of the medial wall
Greater ability to restore heel width
items.e: The limited sinus tarsi approach allows posterior facet reduction with significantly fewer wound breakdowns and infections than the extensile L-shaped lateral incision.

items.q: The most common malunion after a displaced talar neck fracture is:
o: Varus malunion from medial neck comminution
Shortening of the lateral column only
items.e: Medial comminution leads to varus malalignment, which stiffens the subtalar joint and causes lateral foot overload; dual medial and lateral approaches help judge reduction.

items.q: In purely ligamentous Lisfranc (tarsometatarsal) injuries, the RCT by Ly and Coetzee (2006) showed that compared with ORIF, primary partial arthrodesis gave:
o: Better functional scores and fewer secondary procedures
items.e: Primary arthrodesis of the medial two or three TMT joints gave superior AOFAS scores and fewer reoperations than ORIF in purely ligamentous injuries.

items.q: A young patient has an ipsilateral displaced femoral neck fracture and femoral shaft fracture after a motorcycle crash. The usual fixation priority is:
o: Intramedullary nailing of the shaft first, then the neck
Cephalomedullary nail alone without separate neck reduction
Anatomical reduction and stable fixation of the femoral neck first
Fix the shaft and treat the neck non-operatively
items.e: The neck fracture carries the risk of avascular necrosis and nonunion, so it is reduced and fixed first; the shaft is then fixed with a retrograde nail or plate.

items.q: For retrograde nailing of a distal femoral fracture, the correct entry point on the lateral radiograph is:
o: At the anterior cortex of the femoral trochlea
Just anterior to the apex of Blumensaat's line in the intercondylar notch
items.e: The start point lies in the intercondylar notch just anterior to Blumensaat's line (in line with the canal on the AP view), avoiding the PCL origin and the patellofemoral cartilage.

items.q: In a bicondylar tibial plateau fracture, a separate posteromedial coronal fragment is identified on CT. It is best stabilised by:
o: A separate posteromedial approach with a buttress plate
Longer lateral locking screws aimed posteromedially
An anterior medial plate placed on the tibial crest
items.e: Lateral locking screws often fail to capture the posteromedial fragment, which tends to displace in flexion; it is reduced and buttressed through a posteromedial approach.

items.q: In patients aged 75 or over with an isolated displaced olecranon fracture, the RCT by Duckworth et al. (2017) comparing non-operative treatment with tension-band wiring found:
o: No difference in functional outcome, with more complications after surgery
Higher nonunion-related disability after non-operative treatment
Mandatory surgery because of extension weakness
items.e: Function (DASH/Mayo) was similar despite radiographic nonunion in many non-operative patients, while surgery carried a high complication and reoperation rate.

items.q: In Matta's criteria for non-operative management of a displaced acetabular fracture, the roof arc angles measured on the AP, obturator and iliac oblique views should all exceed:
items.e: Roof arc angles above 45° on all three views (or about 10 mm intact subchondral arc on CT) indicate that the weight-bearing dome is intact.

items.q: A burst fracture at L1 has an indeterminate posterior ligamentous complex on MRI and the patient has an incomplete cord injury. The TLICS total and recommendation are:
items.e: Burst morphology scores 2, indeterminate PLC 2 and incomplete cord injury 3, totalling 7; scores above 4 favour surgery.

items.q: In the AOSpine thoracolumbar classification, a purely osseous flexion-distraction (bony Chance) fracture through the posterior elements and vertebral body is classified as:
items.e: B1 is a transosseous disruption of the posterior tension band; B2 involves ligamentous or osseoligamentous disruption; B3 is a hyperextension injury and C a translation injury.

items.q: In the Subaxial Injury Classification (SLIC), an incomplete cord injury with continuous cord compression scores how many points for neurological status?
items.e: An incomplete cord injury scores 3, and continuous cord compression in the setting of a neurological deficit adds 1, giving 4.

items.q: A Levine–Edwards type IIA traumatic spondylolisthesis of the axis (hangman's fracture) shows severe angulation with minimal translation. Which treatment is specifically avoided?
o: Halo vest in extension with compression
items.e: Type IIA is a flexion-distraction injury; traction widens the C2–C3 disc space and worsens displacement, so it is treated by extension and compression in a halo or by surgery.

items.q: During lateral transpsoas lumbar interbody fusion, the risk of lumbar plexus (femoral nerve) injury is highest at:
items.e: The lumbar plexus migrates anteriorly within psoas at caudal levels, so it lies closest to the working corridor at L4–L5, where the iliac crest also limits access.

items.q: Sorensen's radiographic criteria for Scheuermann kyphosis require:
o: Anterior wedging of at least 5° in three or more adjacent vertebrae
Anterior wedging of at least 10° in two adjacent vertebrae
Wedging of at least 5° in a single vertebra with Schmorl nodes
items.e: Classic diagnosis is ≥5° wedging of at least three consecutive vertebrae, usually with thoracic kyphosis above 45°, endplate irregularity and Schmorl nodes.

items.q: A 68-year-old with ankylosing spondylitis has neck pain after a minor fall; cervical radiographs show no fracture. The most appropriate next step is:
o: CT (and MRI) of the whole spine
Soft collar and review in 2 weeks
items.e: Fractures of the ankylosed spine are unstable, easily missed on radiographs and may be non-contiguous, so whole-spine CT, often with MRI, is mandatory.

items.q: After acute traumatic spinal cord injury, AANS/CNS guidelines recommend maintaining mean arterial pressure at:
o: Above 60 mmHg until spinal shock resolves
items.e: Augmenting MAP to 85–90 mmHg for the first week aims to optimise spinal cord perfusion and has been associated with better neurological recovery.

items.q: A patient develops deltoid and biceps weakness on the second day after multilevel posterior cervical decompression. The most likely course of this C5 palsy is:
o: Immediate improvement only after urgent re-exploration
Gradual recovery over months in most patients
items.e: C5 palsy occurs in about 5% of cervical decompressions, often with delayed onset and posterior cord drift, and most cases recover over weeks to months.

items.q: In about 90% of people, the vertebral artery first enters a transverse foramen at the level of:
items.e: The vertebral artery usually passes anterior to the C7 transverse process and enters the foramen transversarium at C6, so anomalous entry at higher levels must be checked before anterior surgery.

items.q: On a lateral cervical radiograph, atlanto-occipital dissociation is suggested when the basion–dens interval exceeds:
items.e: Harris's rule of 12 uses a basion–dens interval or basion–axial interval over 12 mm on radiographs; CT thresholds are lower (about 8.5–10 mm).

items.q: Two randomised sham-controlled trials (Buchbinder; Kallmes, NEJM 2009) of vertebroplasty for painful osteoporotic vertebral fractures showed:
o: Marked superiority over sham at 1 month
Benefit only for fractures older than 1 year
No significant benefit over a sham procedure
Increased adjacent-level fractures as the main finding
items.e: Pain and disability improved similarly in vertebroplasty and sham groups, questioning its routine use.

items.q: The artery of Adamkiewicz most commonly arises:
o: From the right side between T5 and T8
From the left side between L3 and L5
From the vertebral artery at C6
From the left side between T9 and T12
items.e: The great anterior radiculomedullary artery usually arises on the left between T9 and T12 and is relevant to left-sided thoracolumbar approaches.

items.q: A 60-year-old with myelopathy has cervical OPLL that projects beyond the K-line on a neutral lateral radiograph (K-line negative). The appropriate surgical approach is:
o: Anterior decompression or posterior decompression with fusion, rather than laminoplasty alone
Observation, as K-line negative predicts spontaneous improvement
items.e: When OPLL crosses the C2–C7 K-line, posterior cord drift after laminoplasty is insufficient and neurological recovery is poor; anterior decompression or posterior fusion is preferred.

items.q: A far-lateral (extraforaminal) disc herniation at L4–L5 most often compresses the:
items.e: Far-lateral herniations affect the exiting root at that level (L4 at L4–L5), whereas paracentral herniations compress the traversing root (L5).

items.q: A lumbar pedicle subtraction osteotomy typically achieves about how much sagittal correction at a single level?
items.e: A PSO closes a posterior-based wedge through the vertebral body for roughly 30–40° of lordosis; a Smith-Petersen osteotomy gives about 10° per level.

items.q: The Wiltse paraspinal approach to the lumbar spine uses the intermuscular plane between:
items.e: The Wiltse approach splits multifidus medially from longissimus laterally, giving direct access to the facets and transverse processes for far-lateral pathology and pedicle screws.

items.q: A 58-year-old with degenerative cervical myelopathy has an mJOA score of 13. According to AOSpine/CSRS guidelines, management should be:
o: Surgery only if MRI shows cord signal change
Observation, as this score is normal
items.e: mJOA 15–17 is mild, 12–14 moderate and ≤11 severe; surgery is recommended for moderate and severe myelopathy.

items.q: Romosozumab, used for severe postmenopausal osteoporosis, is a monoclonal antibody against a protein secreted mainly by which cell?
items.e: Romosozumab binds sclerostin, which osteocytes secrete to inhibit Wnt/LRP5-6 signalling; blocking it increases bone formation and reduces resorption.

items.q: If the diameter of a solid cylindrical femoral stem is doubled, its bending stiffness increases by a factor of about:
items.e: Bending stiffness is proportional to the area moment of inertia, which varies with radius to the fourth power, so doubling the diameter gives 2^4 = 16 times the stiffness.

items.q: A high-energy tibial pilon fracture has been spanned with an external fixator. Definitive ORIF is usually delayed until:
o: The wrinkle sign returns, typically 10-14 days
items.e: Staged management (span, scan, plan) waits for soft-tissue swelling to settle, shown by the return of skin wrinkles, usually at 1-3 weeks, to reduce wound complications.

items.q: A patient with a cervical spinal cord injury has no motor or sensory function below the lesion except preserved deep anal pressure. By ASIA (ISNCSCI), this injury is:
items.e: Any sacral sparing (S4-5 light touch, pinprick, deep anal pressure or voluntary anal contraction) makes an injury incomplete; sensory sparing without motor function below the level is AIS B.

items.q: Anterior odontoid screw fixation is generally unsuitable in which Grauer subtype of type II odontoid fracture?
o: IIC - fracture line from anteroinferior to posterosuperior, or comminuted
IIB - line from anterosuperior to posteroinferior
items.e: In IIC the fracture plane runs parallel to the screw path (or is comminuted), so lag compression is not possible and posterior C1-C2 fusion is preferred.

items.q: Recombinant BMP-7 (OP-1) received a US FDA humanitarian device exemption for which indication?
o: Acute open tibial shaft fractures treated with an intramedullary nail
Recalcitrant long-bone nonunion where autograft is not feasible
Single-level anterior lumbar interbody fusion with a tapered cage
Routine primary posterolateral fusion in all adults
items.e: OP-1 (BMP-7) had only humanitarian device exemptions, for recalcitrant long-bone nonunion and revision posterolateral lumbar fusion when autograft was unsuitable; the open tibia and ALIF approvals belong to rhBMP-2.

items.q: Dilute povidone-iodine lavage before wound closure in arthroplasty, shown by Brown et al. to reduce early periprosthetic infection, uses which concentration and duration?
items.e: A 0.35% povidone-iodine solution left in the wound for 3 minutes, then irrigated with saline, reduced acute PJI without harming wound healing.

items.q: In Vallier's 'early appropriate care' protocol, which base excess value indicates adequate resuscitation for early definitive fixation?
o: Base excess of -10 mmol/L or better
Base excess of -2 mmol/L or better
Base excess of +5 mmol/L or more
Base excess of -5.5 mmol/L or better (less negative)
items.e: Early appropriate care proceeds to definitive fixation within 36 hours if any one of lactate <4.0 mmol/L, pH 7.25 or more, or base excess -5.5 mmol/L or better is met.

items.q: Compared with the Gallie technique, the Brooks-Jenkins posterior C1-C2 wiring:
o: Uses sublaminar wires under both C1 and C2 with two bone grafts, giving better rotational stability
Uses a single midline graft wired to the C2 spinous process only
Uses transarticular screws instead of wires
items.e: Brooks fusion passes sublaminar wires under C1 and C2 on each side, securing two wedge grafts, so it resists rotation better than the Gallie single midline graft, though sublaminar passage at C2 adds neurological risk.

items.q: Which cervical spine injury pattern is a screening indication for CT angiography for blunt cerebrovascular (vertebral artery) injury under the Denver criteria?
o: Fracture extending into the transverse foramen
Stable anterior wedge fracture of C5 under 10%
items.e: Denver criteria include C1-C3 fractures, subluxation and fractures extending into the transverse foramen, because these can injure the vertebral artery.

items.q: 'Triangular osteosynthesis' for a vertically unstable sacral fracture consists of:
o: Two parallel iliosacral screws at S1 and S2
Anterior symphyseal plate and external fixator
Lumbopelvic (L5 pedicle to iliac) fixation combined with an iliosacral screw
items.e: Schildhauer's triangular osteosynthesis combines vertical lumbopelvic distraction rods with transverse iliosacral screw fixation, giving greater stability against vertical shear than iliosacral screws alone.

items.q: The Taylor spatial frame corrects multiplanar deformities by adjusting:
o: Two hinges placed at the apex of deformity
A single monolateral rail with a distractor
Six telescopic struts connecting two rings
items.e: The Taylor spatial frame is a hexapod: six adjustable struts between two rings allow simultaneous correction in six axes using a computer-generated schedule.

items.q: In distraction osteogenesis, the 'bone healing index' (or lengthening index) is expressed as:
o: Days in the external fixator per centimetre of lengthening
Regenerate width divided by original bone width
items.e: The healing index is total frame time divided by length gained, typically about 30-40 days/cm in children and more in adults.

items.q: A patient with long-standing ankylosing spondylitis has progressive back pain at a mobile segment. Imaging shows destructive changes through the disc and adjacent endplates of an otherwise fused spine. This is:
items.e: An Andersson lesion is an inflammatory or traumatic pseudarthrosis through the disc of an ankylosed spine; it may need fusion if unstable.

items.q: In a patient with a spinal cord injury above T6, autonomic dysreflexia is suspected (severe hypertension, headache, bradycardia). The first step is to:
o: Lay the patient flat and give IV fluids
Sit the patient upright and look for and remove the noxious stimulus, such as a blocked catheter
items.e: Sitting up lowers blood pressure, and the trigger (often bladder distension or bowel impaction) must be removed; short-acting antihypertensives are added if systolic BP stays above about 150 mmHg.

items.q: An elderly woman has increasing back pain weeks after a minor fall, with delayed collapse of a vertebral body (Kummell disease). Which imaging finding is characteristic?
items.e: Kummell disease is avascular necrosis of a vertebral body after minor trauma, showing an intravertebral vacuum cleft (gas on radiograph or CT, fluid on MRI).

items.q: A 72-year-old woman on haemodialysis for end-stage renal disease has osteoporosis. Which serious adverse effect carries an FDA boxed warning for denosumab in this group?
o: Acute kidney injury from tubular necrosis
items.e: In 2024 the FDA added a boxed warning that patients with advanced CKD, particularly on dialysis or with CKD-mineral bone disorder, are at risk of severe hypocalcaemia after denosumab; the CKD-MBD should be assessed first.

items.q: In the AO Spine subaxial cervical classification, a fracture through both the pedicle and the lamina on the same side, detaching the lateral mass from the vertebra, is graded as:
items.e: F1 is a non-displaced small facet fracture, F2 a potentially unstable facet fracture, F3 a floating lateral mass, and F4 a pathological subluxation, perched or dislocated facet.

items.q: On a lateral cervical radiograph, the 'fat C2 sign' (C2 body wider in AP diameter than C3) suggests:
o: A type I odontoid tip fracture
A fracture of the C2 body (atypical hangman's fracture)
items.e: Widening of the C2 body indicates a vertical or coronal fracture through the vertebral body, which is often subtle on radiographs and should prompt CT.

items.q: On axial CT after a flexion injury, a facet articular surface is seen without its opposing facet (the 'naked facet' sign). This indicates:
o: Facet subluxation or dislocation, as in a flexion-distraction injury
items.e: Normally the facets appear as a 'hamburger bun'; an uncovered (naked) facet or reversed bun shows that the facets have perched or dislocated.

items.q: In cortical bone, the scalloped cement (reversal) line that surrounds each secondary osteon marks:
o: The mineralisation front between osteoid and mineralised bone
The boundary between periosteal and endosteal blood supply
The junction of the inner and outer circumferential lamellae
The limit of osteoclastic resorption where new lamellar bone formation began
items.e: The cement line is laid down at the reversal site of the cutting cone where resorption stopped and osteoblasts started forming the new osteon; it is collagen-poor and a site where microcracks are deflected.

items.q: A child has dense, fracture-prone bones on radiographs together with renal tubular acidosis and intracranial calcification. Deficiency of which enzyme explains all three features?
items.e: Carbonic anhydrase II supplies the protons osteoclasts need to dissolve mineral and is also needed for renal acidification; its deficiency gives osteopetrosis with RTA and cerebral calcification.

items.q: Which transcription factor acts downstream of RUNX2 and is essential for osteoblast differentiation, so that knockout mice form a cartilage skeleton but no bone?
items.e: Osterix (SP7) is required after RUNX2 for commitment of pre-osteoblasts to mature osteoblasts; without it no bone matrix is formed despite normal cartilage.

items.q: Campomelic dysplasia, with anterior bowing of the tibiae, hypoplastic scapulae and XY sex reversal, is caused by haploinsufficiency of which master chondrogenic transcription factor?
items.e: SOX9 drives chondrocyte differentiation and type II collagen and aggrecan expression and also testis development, hence skeletal bowing with sex reversal when one copy is lost.

items.q: Stickler syndrome type 2, with high myopia, sensorineural deafness, cleft palate and early-onset arthropathy, is caused by mutation of COL11A1. The main role of type XI collagen in articular cartilage is to:
o: Form the pericellular capsule around chondrocytes
Regulate the diameter of type II collagen fibrils as part of the fibril core
items.e: Type XI collagen co-polymerises within type II fibrils and controls their nucleation and diameter; its loss produces abnormal fibrils in cartilage and the vitreous.

items.q: Which aggrecanase is regarded as the principal enzyme of aggrecan breakdown in osteoarthritis, its knockout protecting mice from surgically induced OA?
items.e: ADAMTS-5 (aggrecanase-2) cleaves aggrecan in the interglobular domain; knockout mice are protected from cartilage proteoglycan loss after joint destabilisation.

items.q: In normal adult articular cartilage, the zone with the HIGHEST proteoglycan concentration and the LOWEST water content is the:
items.e: Proteoglycan content rises and water content falls from the surface to the deep zone, where collagen fibres run perpendicular to the subchondral bone.

items.q: Normal synovial fluid becomes less viscous as the shear rate rises during rapid joint motion. This shear-thinning (non-Newtonian) behaviour is due mainly to:
items.e: Long hyaluronan chains entangle at rest and align under shear, so viscosity falls at high shear rates; lubricin provides boundary lubrication rather than bulk viscosity.

items.q: Osteocytes sense mechanical loading chiefly through:
o: Direct piezoelectric charge on the osteocyte nucleus
Changes in serum calcium during loading
Stretch of the periosteal Sharpey fibres
Fluid flow shear stress in the lacunar-canalicular network
items.e: Loading drives interstitial fluid through canaliculi, creating shear on osteocyte processes; osteocytes respond by reducing sclerostin and signalling bone formation.

items.q: Parathyroid hormone-related peptide (PTHrP) and Indian hedgehog form a feedback loop in the growth plate. The main effect of PTHrP is to:
o: Stimulate vascular invasion of the hypertrophic zone
Induce terminal hypertrophy and type X collagen production
Keep proliferating chondrocytes dividing and delay their hypertrophy
Activate osteoclasts in the primary spongiosa
items.e: Indian hedgehog from pre-hypertrophic cells stimulates periarticular PTHrP, which keeps chondrocytes proliferating and delays hypertrophy, setting the length of the columns.

items.q: Calcitonin, which binds receptors directly on osteoclasts, is secreted by:
o: Parafollicular C cells of the thyroid
Proximal tubular cells of the kidney
items.e: Calcitonin comes from neural-crest-derived parafollicular C cells; it causes osteoclasts to retract and stop resorbing.

items.q: A solid intramedullary nail is replaced by one of identical material whose diameter is 20% larger. Its bending stiffness increases by approximately:
items.e: Bending stiffness of a solid rod is proportional to the area moment of inertia, which varies with radius to the fourth power: 1.2^4 is about 2.1.

items.q: A new screening test for osteomyelitis keeps the same sensitivity and specificity but is applied to a population where the disease is much more prevalent. Compared with before:
o: Positive predictive value falls and negative predictive value rises
Positive predictive value rises and negative predictive value falls
items.e: Predictive values depend on prevalence: as prevalence rises, a positive result is more likely true and a negative result less reliable, while sensitivity and specificity are unchanged.

items.q: A small randomised trial of two fixation methods reports 'no significant difference' in nonunion rates, but enrolled far fewer patients than needed. The most likely error is:
items.e: Failing to detect a difference that really exists is a type II error, made more likely by an underpowered (too small) study.

items.q: All other factors being equal, which change INCREASES the statistical power of a clinical trial?
o: Looking for a smaller effect size
Greater variability in the outcome measure
items.e: Power (1 minus beta) rises with sample size, larger effect size, lower variance and a higher alpha; the other three options all reduce it.

items.q: A study compares deep infection (yes/no) between two antibiotic regimens in 300 arthroplasty patients. The appropriate test to compare the proportions is:
items.e: Comparing categorical outcomes between independent groups uses the chi-square test (or Fisher's exact test when expected counts are small).

items.q: Postoperative pain scores (skewed, ordinal) are compared between two independent groups of patients. The appropriate test is:
items.e: The Mann-Whitney U test is the non-parametric test for two independent groups; Wilcoxon signed-rank is for paired data.

items.q: Oxford Knee Scores, not normally distributed, are measured in the same 40 patients before and after TKA. The appropriate test is:
items.e: Paired, non-normal data from the same subjects are compared with the Wilcoxon signed-rank test, the non-parametric equivalent of the paired t-test.

items.q: Comparing a continuous, normally distributed outcome (blood loss) among THREE independent treatment groups requires:
items.e: One-way ANOVA compares means across three or more independent groups without inflating type I error the way multiple t-tests do.

items.q: On musculoskeletal ultrasound, a normal tendon appears falsely hypoechoic when the beam is not perpendicular to its fibres, mimicking a tear. This artefact is called:
items.e: Anisotropy occurs because the ordered tendon fibres reflect sound back to the probe only when insonated at 90 degrees; tilting the probe restores the normal echogenic pattern.

items.q: In a DXA scan, the Z-score rather than the T-score should be used to report bone density in:
items.e: Z-scores compare with age- and sex-matched controls and are used in children, premenopausal women and men under 50; T-scores are used in postmenopausal women and men aged 50 or more.

items.q: Which of the following is an absolute contraindication to MRI?
o: Metallic foreign body in the orbit from welding
Stainless steel tibial nail inserted 2 years ago
items.e: A ferromagnetic intra-orbital fragment can move and cause blindness; modern orthopaedic implants are not contraindications, though they produce artefact.

items.q: After a period of immobilisation in a cast, which muscle fibre type atrophies first and most in antigravity muscles such as the quadriceps?
items.e: Disuse preferentially affects slow-twitch type I fibres of postural antigravity muscles, which are used continuously in daily activity.

items.q: The antifibrinolytic action of tranexamic acid results from:
items.e: Tranexamic acid is a lysine analogue that occupies plasminogen's lysine-binding sites, so plasmin cannot bind and break down fibrin.

items.q: The FOCUS trial in elderly hip-fracture patients with cardiovascular disease compared a liberal transfusion threshold (Hb below 10 g/dL) with a restrictive one (symptoms or Hb below 8 g/dL). It found:
o: Better walking ability with liberal transfusion
More myocardial infarction with restrictive transfusion leading to early stopping
No difference in death or inability to walk unaided at 60 days
items.e: FOCUS (NEJM 2011) showed a restrictive strategy did not worsen 60-day mortality or function, supporting transfusion for symptoms or Hb below 8 g/dL.

items.q: The PREVENT CLOT trial (NEJM 2023) in over 12 000 operatively treated extremity or pelvic fracture patients compared aspirin 81 mg twice daily with low-molecular-weight heparin. Aspirin was:
items.e: Aspirin was non-inferior to enoxaparin for all-cause death, with similar pulmonary embolism and bleeding rates but slightly more deep-vein thrombosis.

items.q: Microcracks propagating through cortical bone are most often deflected and arrested at:
items.e: Cement lines are weak interfaces that deflect cracks, increasing bone's fracture toughness; this is one reason remodelled osteonal bone resists crack propagation.

items.q: In a basic multicellular unit remodelling cortical bone, the correct order of events is:
items.e: Remodelling begins with activation of osteoclast precursors, followed by resorption, a reversal phase with cement-line deposition, osteoblastic formation and finally quiescence.

items.q: The bone matrix protein most widely used as a serum marker of bone FORMATION is:
o: C-terminal telopeptide of type I collagen (CTX)
items.e: P1NP is cleaved from procollagen as type I collagen is laid down and is the reference formation marker; CTX, TRAP-5b and deoxypyridinoline reflect resorption.

items.q: Teriparatide given once daily stimulates bone formation, but continuous high PTH (as in hyperparathyroidism) causes bone loss. The anabolic effect of intermittent PTH is mediated mainly through:
o: Direct binding to PTH receptors on osteoclasts
Reduced osteoblast apoptosis and activation of bone-lining cells
items.e: Intermittent PTH acts on osteoblast-lineage PTH1 receptors, prolonging osteoblast life, activating lining cells and lowering sclerostin, so formation exceeds resorption.

items.q: Bisphosphonates with a nitrogen side chain such as alendronate and zoledronate inhibit osteoclasts by blocking which enzyme?
items.e: Nitrogen-containing bisphosphonates inhibit farnesyl pyrophosphate synthase in the mevalonate pathway, preventing prenylation of small GTPases needed for osteoclast function.

items.q: A cylindrical tube resists torsion better than a solid rod of the same cross-sectional area because:
o: Its material lies farther from the neutral axis, increasing the polar moment of inertia
It has a higher Young's modulus
Hollow structures have a higher yield stress
It transfers more load to the surrounding bone
items.e: Polar moment of inertia increases with the fourth power of the distance of material from the centre, so a hollow tube is more resistant to torsion for the same mass.

items.q: In a Maisonneuve injury, fixation is usually directed at:
o: Repair of the common peroneal nerve
The syndesmosis, restoring fibular length and rotation in the incisura
items.e: The proximal fibular fracture is generally not fixed (risk to the common peroneal nerve); treatment centres on accurate reduction and stabilisation of the syndesmosis.

items.q: A vertical shear pelvic fracture (Young-Burgess VS) is characterised by:
o: Rotational instability with intact posterior ligaments
Superior displacement of the hemipelvis with complete posterior disruption
items.e: VS injuries are rotationally and vertically unstable, with cephalad displacement of the hemipelvis; they need skeletal traction then posterior fixation.

items.q: In a posterior wall acetabular fracture, the most reliable indicator of hip instability requiring fixation is:
o: Instability on examination under anaesthesia or wall fragment involving more than about 50% of the wall
Any fragment size on plain radiographs
items.e: Fragments involving under 20% of the wall are usually stable and over 50% unstable; in between, EUA under fluoroscopy decides.

items.q: In a pilon fracture, the fibula is often fixed early (as part of staging) because it:
o: Restores length and lateral column alignment
items.e: Fixing the fibula restores length and helps reduce the tibial fragments, although a poorly reduced fibula can block later anatomical tibial reduction.

items.q: A displaced olecranon fracture with articular comminution is fixed with a plate rather than a tension band wire mainly because tension banding would:
o: Endanger the ulnar nerve in the cubital tunnel
Compress the comminuted articular fragments and shorten the trochlear notch
items.e: Tension banding needs an intact, simple fracture to convert tension to compression; with comminution, compression collapses fragments and narrows the greater sigmoid notch, so a plate is used.

items.q: In the AO Spine thoracolumbar classification, a type B2 injury is:
o: Anterior tension band disruption in hyperextension
Posterior tension band disruption through ligaments or bone with or without vertebral body fracture
items.e: B1 is a transosseous (bony Chance) posterior tension-band failure, B2 a ligamentous or osseoligamentous posterior tension-band injury and B3 an anterior tension-band (hyperextension) injury.

items.q: In a patient with ankylosing spondylitis and a cervicothoracic fracture, application of a standard cervical collar in the neutral position may be dangerous because:
o: It may force the kyphotic spine into extension, displacing the fracture
It causes pressure sores in all patients
It cannot be removed for imaging
items.e: The rigid kyphotic spine should be immobilised in its pre-injury position, using sandbags or blocks, as forcing it straight can displace the fracture and injure the cord.

items.q: In ISNCSCI, the 'neurological level of injury' is defined as:
o: The level of the bony fracture
The first segment with any abnormal sensation
The level at which the bulbocavernosus reflex is absent
The most caudal segment with normal sensory and antigravity motor function on both sides, with normal segments above
items.e: The NLI is the lowest segment where both sensory and motor function are normal bilaterally; the key muscle must be grade 3 or more with the segment above grade 5.

items.q: A complete C5 tetraplegic patient can be expected to retain which function?
items.e: C5 supplies deltoid and biceps; wrist extension needs C6, elbow extension C7 and finger flexion C8.

items.q: In a hangman's fracture, why are neurological deficits relatively uncommon?
o: The cord is protected by the dens
The fracture widens the canal at C2
The vertebral artery buffers the cord
items.e: Bilateral pars fractures of C2 separate the posterior arch from the body, enlarging the spinal canal and sparing the cord.

items.q: Before closed reduction of a cervical facet dislocation in an awake, cooperative patient, many surgeons do not insist on MRI because:
o: Neurological monitoring during awake traction can detect deterioration
Disc herniation never occurs in facet dislocation
Reduction is done under general anaesthesia
items.e: In an awake, examinable patient, closed traction reduction is considered safe with serial examination; MRI is needed before reduction under anaesthesia or in obtunded patients.

items.q: The subaxial cervical spine injury classification (SLIC) scores morphology, the disco-ligamentous complex and:
items.e: SLIC adds morphology, DLC integrity and neurology; a total over 4 suggests surgery, under 4 non-operative care.

items.q: In the subaxial cervical spine, the vertebral artery normally enters the transverse foramen at:
items.e: The vertebral artery usually enters the foramen transversarium at C6; it lies in front of the C7 transverse process.

items.q: After anterior cervical discectomy and fusion, the main concern from a postoperative neck haematoma is:
items.e: A rapidly expanding haematoma can compress the airway; the wound must be opened at the bedside if breathing is compromised.

items.q: In cauda equina syndrome, the strongest predictor of good bladder recovery is:
o: Decompression before the onset of painless urinary retention
items.e: Outcomes are best when surgery is done in incomplete CES (CES-I), before established painless retention (CES-R).

items.q: A 55-year-old has a 3-month history of sciatica with an L5 deficit from a disc herniation. Compared with conservative care, discectomy primarily speeds:
items.e: Peul et al. (NEJM 2007) showed earlier surgery gave faster relief of leg pain, but by 1 year outcomes were similar.

items.q: In a randomised trial, deep infection occurs in 8% of controls and 6% of the intervention group. The relative risk reduction is:
items.e: RRR = (8 - 6) / 8 = 0.25; the absolute risk reduction is 2% and the number needed to treat 50.

items.q: A study follows a cohort of smokers and non-smokers forward in time from fracture fixation to compare nonunion. This design is a:
items.e: Exposure is identified first and participants followed for the outcome, which is a cohort design; incidence and relative risk can be calculated.

items.q: The 95% confidence interval for the difference in a functional score between two treatments is -2 to +6 points. If the minimal clinically important difference is 10 points, the result shows:
o: A significant but clinically unimportant difference
The study was underpowered for any conclusion
No clinically important difference has been excluded with reasonable certainty
items.e: The interval crosses zero (not significant) and its upper limit is below the MCID, so an important benefit is unlikely.

items.q: The radiation dose to a surgeon's hands during fluoroscopy is best reduced by:
o: Keeping the hands out of the primary beam
items.e: Direct beam exposure dominates hand dose; lead aprons and thyroid shields do not protect the hands.

items.q: In a three-phase technetium bone scan, the second (blood pool) phase reflects:
o: Soft-tissue hyperaemia in the extracellular space
Arterial perfusion in the first minute
items.e: Phase 1 is the flow study, phase 2 blood pool at about 5 minutes and phase 3 delayed bone uptake at 2-4 hours; osteomyelitis is positive in all three.

items.q: In whole-body imaging of myeloma bone disease, the preferred modality in current guidelines is:
items.e: Whole-body low-dose CT (or PET-CT or whole-body MRI) has replaced the skeletal survey because it detects more lytic lesions.

items.q: Heparin-induced thrombocytopenia (type II) typically occurs:
o: Within hours of first exposure, without thrombosis
5-10 days after starting heparin with a platelet fall of over 50% and thrombosis
items.e: HIT is an immune-mediated (anti-PF4/heparin) reaction causing thrombocytopenia and paradoxical thrombosis; heparin must be stopped and a non-heparin anticoagulant started.

items.q: In a patient with heparin-induced thrombocytopenia needing anticoagulation, an appropriate agent is:
items.e: Direct thrombin inhibitors (argatroban) or fondaparinux are used; warfarin alone early can cause venous limb gangrene.

items.q: Gabapentinoids as part of multimodal analgesia after arthroplasty act by:
o: Binding the alpha-2-delta subunit of voltage-gated calcium channels
items.e: Gabapentin and pregabalin reduce excitatory neurotransmitter release by binding the alpha-2-delta subunit; they may cause sedation in the elderly.

items.q: Ketamine reduces postoperative opioid consumption mainly by:
items.e: Low-dose ketamine blocks NMDA receptors, reducing central sensitisation and opioid tolerance.

items.q: Biological DMARDs such as TNF inhibitors before elective arthroplasty should be:
o: Withheld and surgery scheduled at the end of the dosing cycle
items.e: ACR/AAHKS advise withholding biologics so surgery falls after the last dose's interval, restarting when the wound heals (about 14 days).

items.q: A nerve conduction study after a complete axonal injury will show loss of the distal compound muscle action potential after about:
o: 7-10 days, once Wallerian degeneration is complete
items.e: The distal segment conducts until Wallerian degeneration occurs; testing too early cannot distinguish neurapraxia from axonotmesis.

items.q: Muscle healing after a strain is limited mainly by:
items.e: Satellite cells regenerate fibres, but TGF-beta-driven fibrosis creates scar that limits complete recovery.

items.q: Ligament healing after an isolated MCL tear typically produces tissue that compared with normal ligament is:
o: Weaker with more type III collagen and smaller fibrils
Made mostly of type II collagen
items.e: Healed ligament contains more type III collagen and small-diameter fibrils, with persistent inferior mechanical properties.

items.q: The SI unit used to express effective radiation dose, which accounts for tissue sensitivity and allows comparison of stochastic risk between examinations, is the:
items.e: Absorbed dose is in gray; effective dose, weighted for radiation and tissue type, is in sievert.

items.q: The stiffness of a uniplanar external fixator is increased most by:
o: Increasing the distance between pins within a fragment to nearly touching
Reducing the distance between the bar and the bone
items.e: Moving the bar closer to bone, larger pin diameter, more pins, wider pin spread within each fragment and adding a second bar or plane increase stiffness.

items.q: Patients with extreme pain scores are enrolled in a trial and improve on follow-up regardless of treatment. This is best explained by:
items.e: Extreme measurements tend to move toward the average on repeat measurement, which is why control groups are essential.

items.q: In a cohort, smoking appears to be associated with nonunion, but smokers are also more often diabetic. Diabetes in this situation is a potential:
items.e: A confounder is associated with both exposure and outcome and is not on the causal pathway; it can be adjusted for by stratification or regression.

items.q: Elution of antibiotic from PMMA cement is increased by:
o: Using liquid antibiotic in large volumes
Higher porosity and larger surface area (such as beads)
items.e: Elution depends on porosity and surface area; beads elute more than a solid block, while vacuum mixing reduces porosity and elution.

items.q: Adding more than about 2 g of antibiotic per 40 g packet of cement for a definitive (non-spacer) fixation is avoided because it:
o: Causes the cement to set too slowly to use
Weakens the mechanical strength of the cement
items.e: High-dose antibiotic loading is acceptable for spacers but reduces compressive and fatigue strength in cement used for definitive fixation.

items.q: In skeletal muscle, which fibre type has the highest myosin ATPase activity, glycolytic metabolism and fastest fatigue?
items.e: Type IIx fibres are fast-twitch glycolytic fibres used for brief powerful contractions; type I fibres are oxidative and fatigue-resistant.

items.q: In the thoracic spine, the pedicle is typically narrowest at:
items.e: The narrowest pedicles in the thoracic spine are around T4-T6, which matters for pedicle screw placement.

items.q: Vertebral body augmentation (kyphoplasty) for a painful osteoporotic compression fracture is contraindicated by:
o: Active local infection or retropulsed fragment compressing the canal
items.e: Infection, uncorrectable coagulopathy and retropulsion with neural compromise are contraindications; cement may leak into the canal.

items.q: Bone cement leakage after vertebroplasty most commonly occurs into:
o: The paravertebral veins and disc space
items.e: Leakage is common (often asymptomatic) into veins, the disc and paravertebral tissues; pulmonary cement embolism can occur.

items.q: In a cervical spine with a single-level radiculopathy from soft disc herniation, cervical disc arthroplasty compared with ACDF reduces:
items.e: Several RCTs report lower rates of adjacent-level reoperation with arthroplasty, though heterotopic ossification can develop.

items.q: A new aspiration test for PJI is evaluated in 200 patients: 45 true positives, 5 false negatives, 15 false positives and 135 true negatives. Its sensitivity is:
items.e: Sensitivity = TP/(TP+FN) = 45/50 = 90%.

items.q: A new aspiration test for PJI is evaluated in 200 patients: 45 true positives, 5 false negatives, 15 false positives and 135 true negatives. Its negative predictive value is about:
items.e: NPV = TN/(TN+FN) = 135/140, about 96%.

items.q: In a cohort of 200 smokers, 30 develop nonunion; in 400 non-smokers, 20 develop nonunion. The relative risk of nonunion for smokers is:
items.e: Risk in smokers 30/200 = 15%, in non-smokers 20/400 = 5%; RR = 15/5 = 3.

items.q: In a case-control study, 40 of 100 patients with deep infection and 20 of 100 controls had diabetes. The odds ratio for diabetes is:
items.e: Odds in cases 40/60 = 0.667, in controls 20/80 = 0.25; OR = 0.667/0.25, about 2.67.

items.q: A 70-kg man is in single-leg stance. The abductor moment arm is 5 cm and the body-weight moment arm (from the centre of gravity of the body minus the stance limb) is 15 cm. Ignoring the limb's weight, the abductor force needed is about:
items.e: Balancing moments: abductor force x 5 = body weight x 15, so abductor force is 3 x body weight; joint reaction force is about 4 x body weight.

items.q: A cylindrical specimen with cross-sectional area 2 cm2 is loaded with 1000 N in tension. The stress in the specimen is:
items.e: Stress = force/area = 1000 N / 0.0002 m2 = 5 000 000 Pa = 5 MPa.

items.q: A 100-mm long tendon graft lengthens by 4 mm under load. The strain is:
items.e: Strain = change in length / original length = 4/100 = 0.04 = 4%; it is dimensionless.

items.q: A material that deforms plastically to a large extent before failure (long plastic region on its stress-strain curve) is described as:
items.e: Ductile materials such as stainless steel undergo large plastic deformation; brittle materials such as ceramics and PMMA fail with little plastic deformation.

items.q: A material whose mechanical properties are the same regardless of the direction of loading is:
items.e: Metals are essentially isotropic; bone, ligament and tendon are anisotropic, with properties depending on load direction.

items.q: The maximum recommended dose of plain bupivacaine for a 60-kg adult is about:
items.e: The usual maximum is about 2 mg/kg (max about 150-175 mg) without adrenaline; 2 x 60 = 120 mg.

items.q: Liposomal bupivacaine used in periarticular injection should not be given within about 20 minutes after:
o: Other local anaesthetics such as lidocaine
items.e: Non-bupivacaine local anaesthetics can cause immediate release of bupivacaine from the liposomes, so a delay of 20 minutes is advised.

items.q: Smoking impairs fracture healing mainly by:
o: Nicotine-induced vasoconstriction and reduced osteoblast function
items.e: Nicotine causes vasoconstriction and inhibits osteoblast proliferation; carbon monoxide reduces tissue oxygen, increasing nonunion and infection.

items.q: During lumbar discectomy, breaching the anterior annulus at L4-L5 risks injury to the:
o: Inferior vena cava at the level of T12
items.e: The aortic bifurcation and iliac vessels lie just in front of the L4-L5 disc; vascular injury presents with hypotension and may need emergency laparotomy.

items.q: Facet tropism refers to:
o: Asymmetry in orientation between the left and right facet joints
items.e: Asymmetrical facet orientation may increase rotational stress on the disc and is associated with disc herniation and degenerative spondylolisthesis.

items.q: A synovial facet cyst at L4-L5 typically presents with:
o: Radiculopathy from compression of the traversing nerve root
items.e: Facet cysts often accompany degenerative spondylolisthesis and compress the traversing L5 root in the lateral recess.

items.q: Through the anterior retroperitoneal approach to L5-S1, the structure at risk causing retrograde ejaculation in men is:
items.e: The sympathetic superior hypogastric plexus anterior to the L5-S1 disc mediates closure of the bladder neck; injury causes retrograde ejaculation.

items.q: Oblique lateral interbody fusion (OLIF) differs from the transpsoas approach in that it:
o: Approaches through the corridor between the aorta and the psoas
items.e: OLIF uses the anterior-to-psoas corridor, avoiding psoas splitting and lumbar plexus injury but risking vascular and sympathetic structures.

items.q: During anterolateral plating of the humeral shaft, the nerve to protect at the distal third is the:
o: Radial nerve between brachialis and brachioradialis
items.e: Distally the radial nerve lies in the interval between brachialis and brachioradialis; brachialis is split to protect it.

items.q: Acceptable angulation for a fifth metacarpal neck fracture treated non-operatively is generally up to:
o: 40-70 degrees, provided there is no rotational deformity
Any angulation if there is malrotation
items.e: The mobile fourth and fifth CMC joints compensate for angulation; malrotation (scissoring) is never accepted.

items.q: After a trauma CT, an isolated non-displaced transverse process fracture of L3 in a neurologically intact patient is treated with:
items.e: Isolated transverse process fractures are stable; they are markers of energy, and associated abdominal injuries must be excluded.

items.q: In a tibial shaft fracture treated non-operatively, acceptable alignment includes:
o: Less than 5 degrees varus/valgus, less than 10 degrees sagittal angulation and less than 1 cm shortening
items.e: These criteria help avoid altered knee and ankle loading and cosmetic deformity.

items.q: Gamma irradiation of structural bone allograft at doses above about 25-30 kGy:
o: Has no effect on mechanical properties
items.e: High-dose irradiation damages collagen cross-links and weakens bone allografts, while lower doses do not reliably inactivate viruses.

items.q: Mesenchymal stem cells are defined by the International Society for Cellular Therapy partly by expression of:
items.e: MSCs must be plastic-adherent, express CD73, CD90 and CD105, lack haematopoietic markers (CD34, CD45) and differentiate into bone, cartilage and fat.

items.q: The most appropriate measure of central tendency for length of hospital stay, which is heavily skewed by a few prolonged admissions, is the:
items.e: The median is resistant to outliers and skewness; the mean is pulled toward the long tail.

items.q: The reporting guideline specifically designed for randomised controlled trials is:
items.e: CONSORT covers RCTs; STROBE observational studies, PRISMA systematic reviews and STARD diagnostic accuracy studies.

items.q: FDG-PET imaging works because tumour and inflammatory cells show:
items.e: FDG is taken up by GLUT transporters and phosphorylated, trapping it in metabolically active cells; it is not specific for malignancy.

items.q: Strontium ranelate use declined largely because of an increased risk of:
items.e: European regulators restricted strontium ranelate due to cardiovascular and thromboembolic risks.

items.q: Which class of drug used in the elderly is most strongly associated with increased fracture risk from falls?
items.e: Sedatives impair balance and reaction time, increasing falls and hip fractures.

items.q: Long-term proton pump inhibitor use has been associated with:
items.e: PPIs may reduce calcium absorption, and observational studies show modestly increased hip and vertebral fracture risk.

items.q: A nerve transfer differs from a nerve graft in that it:
o: Bridges a gap with a sensory nerve
Requires the proximal stump of the injured nerve
Uses a nearby expendable motor branch to reinnervate a target close to the muscle
Is only used for sensory reconstruction
items.e: Nerve transfers bring a donor motor axon source close to the target muscle, shortening regeneration distance and time.

items.q: In a randomised trial, an analysis of a subgroup not prespecified in the protocol showing a significant effect should be regarded as:
items.e: Post-hoc subgroup findings are prone to chance (multiple testing) and need confirmation in a separate trial.

items.q: In Klippel-Feil syndrome, which investigation should be routinely performed because of associated anomalies?
items.e: Renal anomalies occur in about one third; hearing assessment and cardiac evaluation are also advised.

items.q: A Chiari I malformation is defined by:
o: Herniation of the brainstem and fourth ventricle
Descent of the cerebellar tonsils at least 5 mm below the foramen magnum
items.e: Tonsillar ectopia of 5 mm or more defines Chiari I, which is associated with syringomyelia and atypical (left thoracic) scoliosis.

items.q: A radial styloid fracture extending into the wrist joint (chauffeur's fracture) is important because it is associated with:
items.e: The radial styloid is the attachment of the radioscaphocapitate ligament; carpal ligament injury and perilunate patterns must be sought.

items.q: Serial casting for a joint contracture works mainly by exploiting which viscoelastic property of soft tissue?
o: Stress relaxation and creep under sustained low load
items.e: Holding tissue at a constant stretch lets stress relax, and sustained load produces creep, gradually lengthening the tissue.

items.q: In a non-inferiority trial, the most important pre-specified element is:
o: A sample size smaller than superiority trials
items.e: The margin defines how much worse the new treatment can be and still be acceptable; both ITT and per-protocol analyses are usually reported.

items.q: The main problem with the 'learning curve' in surgical trials of a new procedure is that:
o: It eliminates the need for randomisation
Early poor results may underestimate the new technique's true effect
items.e: Surgeons early in the learning curve may have more complications, biasing results against the new technique.

items.q: Preoperative intravenous iron for anaemic patients before elective arthroplasty is most useful in:
o: Anaemia of chronic kidney disease only
Iron-deficiency anaemia detected several weeks before surgery
items.e: Patient blood management programmes screen for anaemia early and correct iron deficiency, reducing transfusion.

items.q: An arthroplasty patient develops a fever, rigors and hypotension within minutes of starting a red-cell transfusion. The first step is:
items.e: Suspected acute haemolytic or septic reaction requires stopping the transfusion, maintaining IV access and checking patient and unit identity.

items.q: Hypothermia during long orthopaedic surgery increases:
o: Surgical site infection and blood loss
items.e: Even mild hypothermia impairs coagulation and neutrophil function and causes vasoconstriction, so active warming is recommended.

items.q: The 'ALARA' principle in radiation protection stands for:
items.e: Radiation exposure should be kept as low as reasonably achievable using time, distance and shielding.

items.q: Tarlov cysts are:
o: Synovial cysts of the facet joint
Arachnoid cysts of the cervical spine
Perineural cysts of the sacral nerve roots
items.e: Tarlov cysts arise at the dorsal root ganglion level of sacral roots; most are asymptomatic incidental findings.

items.q: The commonest primary intradural extramedullary spinal tumours are:
items.e: Nerve sheath tumours and meningiomas are the commonest intradural extramedullary tumours; ependymoma is the commonest intramedullary tumour in adults.

items.q: Vertebral haemangioma on MRI typically appears:
o: Bright on both T1 and T2 owing to fat and vascular content
Dark on T1 and bright on T2 with soft-tissue mass in all cases
items.e: Fat-rich haemangiomas are hyperintense on T1 and T2; aggressive haemangiomas with less fat may be T1 iso- or hypointense.

items.q: Rejecting the null hypothesis when it is actually true is a:
o: Type I error, with probability equal to alpha
Type II error, with probability equal to beta
Type I error, with probability equal to power
Type II error, with probability equal to alpha
items.e: A type I error is a false positive; alpha (usually 0.05) is its accepted probability.

items.q: Which surgical scrub or skin preparation is generally recommended before orthopaedic surgery to reduce surgical site infection?
items.e: Alcohol-based chlorhexidine skin preparation lowered SSI compared with povidone-iodine in randomised studies and is recommended by WHO and NICE.

items.q: Laminar airflow in operating theatres works by:
o: Recirculating air through the theatre without filtration
Delivering filtered air unidirectionally to sweep particles away from the wound
Creating negative pressure in the theatre
items.e: Ultraclean ventilation with HEPA-filtered unidirectional flow reduces airborne bacterial counts at the wound.

items.q: The main source of airborne bacteria in the operating theatre is:
o: Skin squames shed by theatre personnel
items.e: People shed skin scales carrying bacteria; limiting door opening and staff numbers reduces contamination.

items.q: Alpha-defensin testing of synovial fluid for PJI is valuable because it:
o: Is highly sensitive and specific and less affected by prior antibiotics
items.e: Alpha-defensin is an antimicrobial peptide released by neutrophils; its accuracy is retained after antibiotic therapy but can be falsely positive with metallosis.

items.q: After an incidental durotomy is repaired, the patient develops positional headache, worse when upright. This is due to:
o: Cerebrospinal fluid leak with intracranial hypotension
items.e: Persistent CSF leaks cause orthostatic headache; bed rest, hydration or a blood patch or re-exploration may be needed.

items.q: Postoperative visual loss after prone spine surgery is most commonly due to:
o: Central retinal artery occlusion from pressure
items.e: Posterior ischaemic optic neuropathy is associated with long procedures, large blood loss, hypotension and prone positioning.

items.q: Pressure on the eye causing central retinal artery occlusion during prone spinal surgery is prevented by:
o: Using a headrest that avoids pressure on the globes
Placing the head below the heart
Using tape on the eyelids only
items.e: Direct ocular compression in the prone position raises intraocular pressure; checking the eyes regularly avoids it.

items.q: The most common causative organism of postoperative spinal wound infection is:
items.e: S. aureus predominates; late infections with indolent organisms such as C. acnes occur around instrumentation.

items.q: Adjacent segment degeneration after lumbar fusion is most commonly seen at:
items.e: Increased stress at the cranial adjacent segment accelerates degeneration, more so in long fusions and with sagittal malalignment.

items.q: In adult degenerative scoliosis, the apex of the curve is usually located at:
items.e: De novo degenerative scoliosis typically has a lumbar apex around L2-L3 with lateral listhesis and associated stenosis.

items.q: Spinal cord injury without radiographic abnormality (SCIWORA) occurs mainly in children because:
o: The paediatric spine is more elastic than the cord
The cord is larger relative to the canal
items.e: The flexible immature spine can deform beyond the cord's tolerance and then return to normal alignment, leaving no fracture.

items.q: The Henry (volar) approach to the radial shaft uses the interval proximally between:
o: Extensor carpi radialis brevis and EDC
Flexor carpi radialis and palmaris longus
items.e: Proximally the interval is BR and pronator teres, distally BR and FCR; the radial artery and superficial radial nerve are protected.

items.q: In a trial, the investigators calculate the sample size before starting. The four inputs needed are alpha, power, the expected effect size and:
o: The variability (standard deviation) of the outcome
